n1: Every short in this series came off one production line. A script names the scenes and the narration. Then the same steps run every time: voice the lines, draw the boards, compose the cut, and check it. For the first eighteen figures, those steps ran by hand. Steps like that are a recipe, so now they're a Keelson workflow. Whether the cut is any good is a judgment, so that part is a gate.

n5: A check can measure a cut: its length, its loudness, any long silence. It can't see a cursor in the wrong place, or a caption over the answer. So QA writes a review page, a contact sheet of nine frames from across the cut, the numbers, and the script, and the run waits on it.
